cohort: 185 pregnancies in women with neuropsychiatric illnesses or substance abuse compared to 4907 pregnancies in healthy women
finding: Maternal neuropsychiatric illness was associated with a higher rate of previous abortions and earlier births, but no difference in birth weight, head circumference, or Apgar scores compared to healthy controls.
mod_finding: The study found that the rate of cesarean section was significantly higher in women with neuropsychiatric illness compared to controls.
gest_age: Not specified, but children of mothers with neuropsychiatric illness were born at lower gestational ages
